title: Fresh Mint and Chocolate Cookie Ice Cream (No Egg)
changes_from_base: Fresh mint steeped in the warm dairy and chopped chocolate sandwich cookies replace the strawberries; no extract or colouring, so the ice cream stays ivory.
summary: Real mint leaves steeped in warm cream give this ivory ice cream a fresh, garden flavour that extract cannot match, with crunchy chocolate cookie pieces folded through.

ingredients.item: light corn syrup or glucose syrup
fine sea salt or table salt
fresh mint leaves (about 2 large bunches), roughly torn

steps.title: Steep the mint
steps.text: Bring the cream, milk, sugar, syrup and salt to a bare simmer in the saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Take off the heat, push in the torn mint and cover for 30 min.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pour through the sieve into the jug, pressing hard on the leaves to get every bit of flavour, then throw the leaves away. Cool and chill for at least 4 h, or overnight for a stronger mint taste.

steps.title: Prepare the cookies
steps.text: Break the cookies into pieces about the size of a fingernail and keep them in the freezer while the base churns.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn the cold mint base for 20-30 min, until thick and creamy.

steps.title: Fold and freeze
steps.text: Fold the frozen cookie pieces through quickly, pack into the container, cover the surface and freeze for at least 4 h.

tips: Spearmint gives a sweet, rounded taste; peppermint is sharper.
Steep overnight in the fridge, then strain, for a stronger mint flavour.
Freeze the cookie pieces first so they stay crisp instead of going soggy.
storage: Keep covered with baking paper pressed on the surface in the freezer for up to 2 weeks. Soften for 10 min in the fridge before scooping.
